title: Enemy Bot AI for my "Quaketroid" being developed in my custom engine
author: Sencha-Games
selftext:
Hey guys! Last time I posted my engine, I promised my next post would be footage from its flagship game, and behold! 

  
Loss Function 

  
It's still obviously early in development, but the mechanics are coming along nicely. What I like about the engjne is how easily this all fell into place pnce it was time to make the game. The engine provides several ganeplay frameworks that make this kind of gameplay much essier to implement, like data driven ability systems and inventory/equipment. 

So what is Loss Function? Personally, I describe it as Metroid Prime but with Quake-like combat. The story is about an AI system reconstructing a girl to investigate the cause of her own death, only for the reconstruction to find herself hunted by a peer to peer hivemind that's planning on taking over Cyberspace. 

  
During these past couple weeks, I've been focused on making movement and combat feel good. I modelled the enemy AI after Quake 3 bots, which use a combination of fuzzy logic and environmental queries to strategize and make decisions. 

  
The soldiers in this video prefer to disperse and maintain high ground over the player. 

  
You might have noticed that green guy at the beginning who shoots a beam st the wall and moves closer. I call him the Threader. Needless to say, his model is placeholder, but his AI also still needs some work. He's an agressive enemy type who can hookshot at the player to damage them, or pull himself closer to you,  navigating freely around the levels. I've had some fun fighting him in snaller arenas, but he still needs to be tuned to be more aggressive. 

  
While the game itself isn't open source, and won't be until after release, you can check out the engjne here, and do basically whatever you want with it. It's still a young project, so there is still a short checklist of features that aren't complete, some bugs  and memory safety issues I'm aware of and getting to when I can. I update the repo almost every day, and I've been working on it consistently since March. 

[https://github.com/GavynBryan/Sencha](https://github.com/GavynBryan/Sencha)

Since Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2 have gotten so efficient at building games from scratch, I'm not sure iff I can convince you to use Sencha instead of Javascript + ThreeJs, but the main thing I've been designing the engine around is making gameplay iteration and level design fast and enoyable, while still providing elegant architecture underneath like archetypal ECS and explicit dependency wiring.
